 NOTE TO THE TEACHER:
 Included in this document are:
 1. Guidelines for administration
 2. Suggested Timelines
 3. Assessment task
 4. Scoring rubric
 5. Assessment score sheet
1. Guidelines for administration
 The School Based Assessment task has been developed as a step by step guideline to learners.
 • This assessment is an individual performance.
 • The activity is to be done in class during the term.
 • It is important that you guide the learners through the various steps of the task to ensure
 active and creative participation by all learners.
 • Review the scoring rubrics with the learners before they begin the assessment so that they
 understand what will be expected of their final art work.
 • Ensure the completed work is carried out by each learner to completion.
 • The assessment task has been provided on page 4.
 • Provide the learners with the assessment task and scoring rubrics on page 4 and 5 (this can
 be printed, downloaded in the learners’ digital devices or written on the blackboard).
 • When you are administering the assessment, learners may ask questions to clarify the
 process. You should encourage them to ask questions at any time throughout the
 execution of the task.
 Preparation for Administering the Assessment
 Tools & Materials required for this performance assessment:
 • Old carton boards, newspaper, magazines, exercise books ( reuse of materials is
 encouraged and to be collected/ assembled by each learner)
 • Old wires, sisal twine or thread,
 • Tempera paints or watercolours,
 • Paint brushes or sponge or old rugs,
 • Glue (this can be extracted from plants), or masking tape or cello tape.
 All these materials can be improvised where applicable. Schools are encouraged to reuse
 materials.

2. Timelines for the project
 Learners may have as much time as they need to complete the task. The timelines suggested
 here are meant only as a guide, and you may shorten or lengthen them depending on
 individual learner’s.
 The following is a four-week suggested timeline:
 FROM THE DAY PROJECT IS RECEIVED AS PER KNEC GUIDELINES
 WEEK 1
 • The teacher provides the learners with the task and reads it aloud. The learners
 may ask questions. The teacher answers any questions.
 • The learners are guided to begin making sketches on the task as they
 familiarize with the task requirements. The teacher further guides the learners
 on how to carry out the task, collect and store all the materials and tools
 required.
 WEEK 2
 • The learners continue making sketches and improving on their pieces.
 • The teacher ensures all the learners clearly label there sketches as they
 progress to include name and date; each should place every sketch in their
 assessment portfolios. ( These can also be photographed and stored in an e
 portfolio)
 • The learners begin assembling their pieces
 NOTE: Do not buy portfolios/folders; improvise with materials that are
 locally available.
 WEEK 3 - 4
 • The learners continue working until they complete their artworks, document
 (take photographs and short videos) the learners work as they progress.
 • The teacher collects the final artworks and scores using the rubrics, record the
 performance levels e.g. 4, 3, 2, 1 in the project assessment score sheet
 provided at the end of this document before keying the scores in the KNEC
 CBA portal. Once the scores are uploaded, handover the project score sheet,
 documented evidence together with the all the learners work to the Head
 teacher/Senior teacher for secure storage as evidence for future
 reference.
 NOTE:
 • Some of the learners may require more time to complete the task than others; you may
 give these learners time to finish.
 • While some may experience difficulties, break the tasks down into manageable steps.
 • Ensure that all learners have an opportunity to complete the tasks.
 • Learners with visual impairment could do the same tasks using touch to determine the
 different textures and shapes.

3. ASSESMENT TASK:
 “Puppets are used for storytelling and role playing. Puppets may be used for entertainment, to
 teach, and highlight pertinent issues in society”.
 You are required to give a talk to your classmates on the best practices on the forthcoming
 school elections. Construct a marionette to be used to pass the message.
 a. The marionette should take the shape of a human form,
 b. It should have a height of between 20 cm or 30 cm,
 c. The height excludes the strings that will be used for moving the marionette,
 d. Make sketches of the marionette that will guide on how the final piece will look like,
 e. Using old cardboards, newspapers, wrapped around wires or twined sisal or thread construct
 the marionette,
 f. Attach the manipulation strings and holder,
 g. Finish the marionette by painting and dress it up.
